issues.legal_issue: A constitutional court may not order restoration of possession of disputed mining land without determining whether the claimant has a legal right to the land and whether the claimed right extends to the area in question.
material_facts: The original mining lease expired in 1947, and whether it was effectively renewed was disputed.
The company claimed rights through a later assignment, but it was not a party to the agreement that recognized the earlier lessee, and the legal effect of the assignment was unresolved.
The company sought possession of a virgin area that it was not shown to have physically occupied or worked.
The High Court left title and legal interest unresolved but ordered the authorities to put the company in possession of the virgin area.
The Supreme Court concluded that the relevant questions about renewal, assignment, and rights in the claimed area had to be examined before possession could be ordered.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order was set aside and the matter remanded for re-adjudication, including examination of the company’s legal interest and right to the claimed area.
issues.legal_principle: Relief under Article 226 that directs restoration of possession must be supported by an established legal entitlement to the property and to the particular area claimed; where that entitlement depends on unresolved questions about renewal, assignment, or the scope of possession, those questions must be examined before relief is granted. The statutory framework discussed included Sections 4 and 13 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948, Rules 26 and 28-A of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949, and Sections 4 and 10 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957. Century Spinning & Manufacturing Co. Ltd. v. The Ulhasnagar Municipal Council and Union of India v. Indo Afghan Co. were cited by counsel, but the Court did not rely on or decide their application.

predicates.constitutional_writ_for_possession: The claimant sought an order in a constitutional writ proceeding directing restoration or protection of possession.
predicates.legal_entitlement_unadjudicated: The claimant’s legal entitlement to the property or claimed area depended on matters that the court had not determined.
predicates.claimed_area_possession_unestablished: The claimant had not established physical possession of the particular area for which restoration was ordered.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks possession relief in a constitutional writ proceeding and either the legal entitlement or possession of the claimed area remains unestablished, the possession order is set aside and the case is remanded.
